text:
maria-ops: FYI getting repeated customer reports of high 503s + latency spikes on dedicated pool eu-west-2 since 08:00 UTC :eyes:
aj: Seen a few alerts. Looks like autoscaler keeps oscillating between 4 and 8 instances for pool-dedicated-eu-west. CPU and GPU utilization bounce a lot.
autoscaler-bot: [08:03:21] pool-dedicated-eu-west scale_up -> 8 (trigger: queue_depth > 120 for 90s)
autoscaler-bot: [08:06:58] pool-dedicated-eu-west scale_down -> 4 (trigger: cpu_avg < 35% for 60s)
sam: logs show a bursty tenant (tenant-id: brightbox) sending many short requests that have small seq lengths but cause cache churn. KV cache miss rate spikes correlate with the up/down pattern.
leo: Sharing a short metric dump:
```
time, queue_depth, cpu_avg, kv_miss_pct
08:02, 85, 62, 12
08:04, 210, 78, 55
08:05, 40, 30, 10
08:06, 180, 70, 48
08:08, 35, 28, 9
```
diana: That looks like a pendulum. Queue depth bursts push scales up, then the short-lived work drains and autoscaler cuts capacity immediately, then cached state is lost and subsequent bursts hit cold caches -> expensive.
maria-ops: Also seeing client 429s for some customers during down-phase. Billing flagged because they retried aggressively and racked up tokens. Customer ops pinged.
aj: Repro idea: run a scripted burst against a dedicated pool with a mix of short requests that flush KV cache and see if we can reproduce oscillation.
sam: Quick repro done in staging @ 08:25: we saw identical oscillation pattern within 12 minutes. Attaching command we used:
```
for i in {1..600}; do curl -s -X POST https://staging-api.redwood/v1/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-open-1","input":"short text"}' &
sleep 0.1
done
```
leo: Why is scale_down threshold so aggressive? cpu_avg < 35% for 60s seems fine for steady traffic but not for bursty. Need hysteresis or cooldown.
autoscaler-bot: Current config: min_replicas=2, max_replicas=16, scale_up_cooldown=30s, scale_down_cooldown=60s, scale_up_step=+4, scale_down_step=-50%
diana: Proposed mitigation: increase scale_down_cooldown to 180s, require sustained low queue_depth and low kv_miss_pct to downscale, and add a tenant isolation cap so one noisy tenant can't trigger full fleet changes.
maria-ops: Also consider a soft reservation (warm slots) for tenants with high short-burst patterns. That would avoid cold KV misses.
aj: I'll open a quick hotfix: bump scale_down_cooldown to 180s for pool-dedicated-eu-west and reduce scale_up_step to +2 to dampen overshoot. Pushing in 5m and will monitor.
oncall-bot: Deploy scheduled by aj at 08:34:12 UTC — change: autoscaler config for pool-dedicated-eu-west (scale_down_cooldown=180s, scale_up_step=2).
sam: After change, early signs look better; oscillation amplitude down, queue_depth spikes still exist but we stay at 6 replicas more often.
leo: Need follow-ups: (1) add kv_miss_pct as a downscale inhibitor, (2) tenant-level throttles/caps, (3) evaluate pre-warming cache on up-scale event (retain subtree KV).
diana: For (3) maybe implement a grace window where on scale_down we mark replicas as tombstoned for Xs to allow KV rehydration when scaled up again.
maria-ops: Customer support update: told affected customers we applied mitigations and are monitoring. Billing team notified to review retry-related charges.
aj: Opening a JIRA: SRE-1248 "Reduce autoscale pendulum for dedicated-eu-west; add KV-aware downscale inhibitors". Assigning to eng-runtime + eng-sre.
sam: Adding reproduction notes + staging script into the ticket.
maria-ops: Thanks everyone. Keep alerts loud if it spikes again. :thumbsup:
leo: Also let's add a short-runbook snippet for oncall to change cooldown quickly if needed (runbook PR incoming).
oncall-bot: Incident resolved? No — monitoring for 60m.
maria-ops: last update 09:10 UTC: metrics stable, no new 503s from reported tenants. I'll close the customer-facing thread after 2 hours if stable.
aj: leaving notes: consider making scale_down_step absolute min (eg never drop below 50% of current) to prevent sudden halfing when small pools.
sam: TL;DR: noisy-short-burst tenant -> KV cache churn -> autoscaler reacts to transient queues -> aggressive downscales remove warm capacity -> repeat. Mitigations applied: increased cooldown, smaller scale-up steps, follow-up tickets for KV-aware inhibitors and tenant isolation.
